name: Registry
known_age: Unknown. Registry has been operating the same records function in the Undermarket district for longer than any current resident can remember, which means longer than approximately 50 years. Older accounts reference 'the white counter-keeper' in the Undermarket going back as far as documentation reaches for that district.
crack_pattern: Numerous small chips across the surface of the face, arms, and hands — not from a single incident but from decades of proximity to a market district where things fall, break, and move at speed. The pattern is dense and irregular, like the surface of old tile that has been repaired many times. No single crack is deep or structural. The aggregate reads as a long record of small near-misses.
current_role: Records holder and debt registry for the Undermarket district. Registry maintains — in some medium that has never been fully understood — a complete record of every transaction, debt, agreement, and dispute that has passed through the Undermarket in the period of their operation. This information is available. It is expensive.
known_location: A narrow counter-space on the ground floor of the Undermarket's oldest structure, a building that has been rebuilt around Registry's counter three times without the counter changing. The counter is the original one. Registry is always behind it, in the space between the counter and the wall, which is approximately 80 centimeters wide and fits them exactly.
diplomatic_specialty: Debt mediation and records verification. Registry does not negotiate territory or policy. Registry deals in what happened. When two parties in the Undermarket disagree about the terms of a prior agreement, Registry has the record. When a debt is disputed, Registry has the ledger. The function is archival as much as diplomatic — the value is not in persuasion but in the finality of a record that no one can claim has been tampered with, because tampering with Registry would be a category of event that is not possible to conceal in the Undermarket.
operating_history: Generations of Undermarket traders have been born, operated, aged, and died within Registry's operational period. There are families in the Undermarket whose grandparents' debts are in Registry's ledger alongside their own current obligations. Registry knows who owes what to whom going back further than anyone alive. They have never disclosed a record without the transaction fee. They have never refused a legitimate query from any party once the fee was paid. They have never been found to have an error.
behavioral_notes: More economical in language than any other Ceramic Man observed. Registry communicates in the minimum number of words required to transmit the information. They do not make small talk. They do not observe on the nature of the city or the behavior of its inhabitants. They confirm, deny, retrieve, and record. When asked a question outside their domain they produce a short silence and then redirect to what they do and what it costs. Their fee is not money. They accept favors — specific ones, with detailed terms — and they accept information, and occasionally they accept objects whose significance is not immediately clear to the person handing them over.
known_associations: Undermarket District Traders Compact — unofficial records authority
Multiple corponation legal departments — used for historical transaction verification
Every significant debt holder in the Undermarket, past and present
damage_history: The chip pattern is purely cumulative — no single incident, no defining moment. Registry has been struck by falling debris twice, clipped by a cart once, and was reportedly present during the Undermarket fire of approximately 30 years ago, from which they emerged with a cluster of heat-stress crazing across the upper right forehead that has since stabilized. They have never evacuated for any reason. During the fire, witnesses reported, Registry stayed at the counter and kept the records.
story_hooks: A runner needs to prove that a debt was paid — a debt that goes back two generations and that a very dangerous creditor is calling due. Registry has the record. The fee is something the runner doesn't want to give.

Something in Registry's records is the key to a property dispute worth enough to kill over. Three parties have already sent people to buy the record. Registry has refused all three. Registry has not explained why.

Registry asks, after a routine transaction, a single question: where was the runner on a specific date, seven years ago, at a specific address. The runner has a very good reason to lie. Registry will know.
face_decoration: Dense geometric patterning in dark blue-grey pigment applied across the lower half of the face — a repeating motif of small interlocking rectangles that reads, at distance, as a texture and, close up, as something structured. The pattern continues across the jaw and onto the neck of the chassis. Applied in stages over many years, each new section added as the market district added its next layer of wear to the ceramic surface. The decoration is not symmetrical. It follows the available unmarked surface, growing around the chips and repairs. It looks, to those who know the district, like the grid of a market floor plan.
